
@tbl-trip-purpose-replacement distinguishes purpose-specific substitution rates from absolute volumes. `r top_volume_purposes$purpose[1]` and `r top_volume_purposes$purpose[2]` contribute the largest replaceable volumes, together accounting for `r sprintf("%.2f", sum(top_volume_purposes$total_replaceable)/1e6)` million retained car-person trips per day. Regionally, `r top_volume_regions$region[1]` and `r top_volume_regions$region[2]` account for the highest absolute volumes of replaceable trips (`r sprintf("%.0f", top_volume_regions$total_replaceable[1]/1000)`k and `r sprintf("%.0f", top_volume_regions$total_replaceable[2]/1000)`k respectively), reflecting their larger populations and trip densities. However, substitution rates are highest in smaller regions, with `r highest_rate_region$region` achieving `r sprintf("%.1f", highest_rate_region$rate)`%, suggesting that targeted charger deployment in lower-density areas could help realise substitution potential that distance and population size alone do not preclude.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-trip-purpose-replacement
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Replaceable trip volumes and substitution rates by purpose across Scotland's seven transport regions. Scotland columns show aggregate car trips, replaceable trips (thousands), and substitution rate. Regional columns show substitution rate (%) for each transport partnership."
#| message: false
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

regions <- c("HITRANS", "Nestrans", "SESTRAN", "SPT", "SWESTRANS", "Tactran", "ZetTrans")

all_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(regions, function(r) {
    path <- opath(r, "replaceable_trips_by_purpose.csv")
    if (file.exists(path)) {
        df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        names(df)[1] <- "purpose"
        df$region <- r
        df
    } else {
        NULL
    }
}))

if (is.null(all_data) || nrow(all_data) == 0) {
    cat("Note: No replaceable trip data available. Table will be generated after regional analyses are run.")
} else {
    scotland <- all_data |>
        group_by(purpose) |>
        summarise(
            car_trips = sum(car_trips),
            replaceable_trips = sum(replaceable_trips),
            .groups = "drop"
        ) |>
        mutate(rate_scotland = ifelse(car_trips > 0, replaceable_trips / car_trips * 100, 0))

    regional_rates <- all_data |>
        select(purpose, region, replacement_rate_pct) |>
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = region, values_from = replacement_rate_pct)

    # Ensure all region columns exist (fill missing regions with 0)
    for (r in regions) {
        if (!r %in% names(regional_rates)) {
            regional_rates[[r]] <- 0
        }
    }

    tbl <- scotland |>
        left_join(regional_rates, by = "purpose") |>
        arrange(desc(rate_scotland)) |>
        select(purpose, car_trips, replaceable_trips, rate_scotland, all_of(regions))

    region_abbrev <- c("HIT", "NES", "SES", "SPT", "SWE", "TAC", "ZET")

    tbl_display <- tbl |>
        mutate(
            car_trips = sprintf("%.1f", car_trips / 1000),
            replaceable_trips = sprintf("%.1f", replaceable_trips / 1000),
            rate_scotland = sprintf("%.1f", rate_scotland),
            across(all_of(regions), ~ sprintf("%.1f", ifelse(is.na(.x), 0, .x)))
        )

    purpose_width_latex <- "4cm"
    purpose_width_html <- "240px"

    if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
        kable(
            tbl_display,
            format = "latex",
            col.names = c(
                "Purpose", "Trips (k)", "Repl. (k)", "Rate",
                region_abbrev
            ),
            align = c("l", rep("r", 10)),
            booktabs = TRUE
        ) |>
            kable_styling(
                font_size = 9,
                latex_options = c("hold_position", "scale_down"),
                full_width = TRUE
            ) |>
            column_spec(1, width = purpose_width_latex)
    } else if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
        kable(
            tbl_display,
            col.names = c(
                "Purpose", "Trips (k)", "Repl. (k)", "Rate",
                region_abbrev
            ),
            align = c("l", rep("r", 10))
        ) |>
            kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
            column_spec(1, width = purpose_width_html)
    } else {
        kable(
            tbl_display,
            col.names = c(
                "Purpose", "Trips (k)", "Repl. (k)", "Rate",
                region_abbrev
            ),
            align = c("l", rep("r", 10))
        )
    }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: chaining-results-v4
#| include: false
r2_chaining <- read.csv(file.path(r2_results_dir, "chaining.csv"))
r2_chaining_geometry <- unique(r2_chaining[c(
    "region", "home_subset_volume", "collinear_failure", "opposed_failure"
)])
stopifnot(
    nrow(r2_chaining_geometry) == 7L, !anyDuplicated(r2_chaining_geometry$region),
    setequal(r2_chaining_geometry$region, r2_oa_counts$region),
    all(is.finite(r2_chaining_geometry$home_subset_volume)),
    all(r2_chaining_geometry$home_subset_volume > 0),
    all(r2_chaining_geometry$collinear_failure == 0),
    all(is.finite(r2_chaining_geometry$opposed_failure)),
    all(r2_chaining_geometry$opposed_failure >= 0 & r2_chaining_geometry$opposed_failure <= 1)
)
r2_opposed_range <- sprintf(
    "%.1f--%.1f", 100 * min(r2_chaining_geometry$opposed_failure),
    100 * max(r2_chaining_geometry$opposed_failure)
)
r2_opposed_national <- weighted.mean(
    r2_chaining_geometry$opposed_failure,
    r2_chaining_geometry$home_subset_volume
)
r2_chaining_totals <- aggregate(cbind(
    baseline_volume, potential_volume, immediate_volume,
    home_subset_volume, loss_volume, adjusted_potential_volume, adjusted_immediate_volume
) ~
    exposure + failure, r2_chaining, sum)
r2_chaining_totals$adjusted_pct <- 100 * r2_chaining_totals$adjusted_potential_volume /
    r2_chaining_totals$baseline_volume
r2_home_share <- r2_chaining_totals$home_subset_volume[1] / r2_metrics$baseline_volume
r2_chain_floor <- min(r2_chaining_totals$adjusted_pct)
```

The substitution rates above treat each trip as an independent leg. The chaining scenarios apply losses only to screened trips with home charging and one-way distance at most 40 km. This subset contributes `r sprintf("%.1f", 100*r2_home_share)` percentage points of the national denominator. It is not the entire theoretical numerator. The adjusted share is $S_{adj}=S_0-E\phi S_H$, where $S_H$ is that subset's weighted share. The transferred exposure settings $E=0.23$--$0.29$ and failure settings $\phi=0.25$--$1$ are assumptions, not estimates of Scottish tours. @tbl-chaining-bound reports these conditional outcomes. The lowest reported share assumes that trips outside the selected subset remain unaffected. Additional chaining losses could reduce it further.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-chaining-bound
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Conditional chaining-loss scenarios for the home-chargeable, AP-screened subset at distances <=40 km. Each interval varies exposure from 0.23 to 0.29 at the specified failure fraction. Other trips remain unchanged. These scenarios do not bound all daily-tour feasibility."
r2_chain_display <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(unique(r2_chaining_totals$failure)), function(phi) {
    x <- r2_chaining_totals[r2_chaining_totals$failure == phi, ]
    data.frame(
        `Failure fraction` = phi, `Theoretical share (%)` =
            sprintf("%.1f--%.1f", min(x$adjusted_pct), max(x$adjusted_pct)),
        `Capacity-sufficient share (%)` = sprintf(
            "%.1f--%.1f",
            min(100 * x$adjusted_immediate_volume / x$baseline_volume),
            max(100 * x$adjusted_immediate_volume / x$baseline_volume)
        ), check.names = FALSE
    )
}))
r2_full_width_table(r2_chain_display, digits = 2, font_size = 11)
```





### EV type assignment and vehicle suitability

```{r}
#| label: compute-ev-type-data
#| echo: false
#| message: false
redistribute_mixed <- function(two_pct, four_pct, mixed_pct) {
    two_pct <- ifelse(is.na(two_pct), 0, two_pct)
    four_pct <- ifelse(is.na(four_pct), 0, four_pct)
    mixed_pct <- ifelse(is.na(mixed_pct), 0, mixed_pct)

    base_total <- two_pct + four_pct
    if (base_total <= 0) {
        return(c(two = 50, four = 50))
    }

    c(
        two = two_pct + mixed_pct * (two_pct / base_total),
        four = four_pct + mixed_pct * (four_pct / base_total)
    )
}

regional_ev_breakdown <- lapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) {
    redistribute_mixed(
        as.numeric(x$executive_summary$ev_type_breakdown$two_seater_pct),
        as.numeric(x$executive_summary$ev_type_breakdown$four_seater_pct),
        as.numeric(x$executive_summary$ev_type_breakdown$mixed_type_pct)
    )
})

ev_type_comparison <- data.frame(
    Region = sapply(available_regions, format_region_name),
    `2-Seater (%)` = vapply(regional_ev_breakdown, function(x) x[["two"]], numeric(1)),
    `4-Seater (%)` = vapply(regional_ev_breakdown, function(x) x[["four"]], numeric(1)),
    check.names = FALSE
)

# Calculate Scotland-wide trip-weighted EV type percentages after
# proportionally redistributing any legacy mixed share.
scotland_ev_totals <- data.frame(
    two_seater = 0,
    four_seater = 0
)

for (region in available_regions) {
    conversion <- regional_data[[region]]$conversion_potential$final_conversion_potential
    breakdown <- regional_ev_breakdown[[region]]
    scotland_ev_totals$two_seater <- scotland_ev_totals$two_seater +
        (conversion * breakdown[["two"]] / 100)
    scotland_ev_totals$four_seater <- scotland_ev_totals$four_seater +
        (conversion * breakdown[["four"]] / 100)
}

total_ev <- scotland_ev_totals$two_seater + scotland_ev_totals$four_seater
if (total_ev <= 0) {
    scotland_ev_pct <- list(two_seater = 50, four_seater = 50)
} else {
    scotland_ev_pct <- list(
        two_seater = (scotland_ev_totals$two_seater / total_ev) * 100,
        four_seater = (scotland_ev_totals$four_seater / total_ev) * 100
    )
}
```

@tbl-ev-type-regional reveals that `r sprintf("%.1f", scotland_ev_pct$four_seater)`% of Scotland's replaceable trips are suited to 4-seater frugal EVs and `r sprintf("%.1f", scotland_ev_pct$two_seater)`% to 2-seater configurations, after proportionally redistributing the legacy mixed category across the two concrete vehicle classes. Four-seater dominance was most pronounced in family-oriented regions such as Nestrans (`r sprintf("%.1f", ev_type_comparison[ev_type_comparison$Region == format_region_name("Nestrans"), "4-Seater (%)"])`%) and Tactran (`r sprintf("%.1f", ev_type_comparison[ev_type_comparison$Region == format_region_name("Tactran"), "4-Seater (%)"])`%), where larger household sizes and multi-occupant commuting patterns favour greater passenger capacity.

```{r}
kable(ev_type_comparison,
    format = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "latex" else "pipe",
    booktabs = TRUE, longtable = FALSE,
    digits = 1,
    align = c("l", "r", "r"),
    row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
        sapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) x$executive_summary$charging_constraint_pct),
        trip_weights

# These calculations are handled elsewhere in the document
```

Charging infrastructure accessibility constrains whether trips within 80 km effective range can convert from ICE to frugal EV, with spatial accessibility scoring confirming the concentration of accessible provision in urban areas [@Potoglou2023]. The following subsections examine the spatial distribution of charging provision, the alignment of that supply with the frugal EV target market, and the resulting constraint landscape that limits substitution potential. The area-level accessibility and capacity-factor figures describe spatial provision. Trip volumes $N$ are partitioned using the physical-station charger-hour capacity test.

### Spatial distribution and accessibility patterns



@fig-charging-infrastructure-map presents Scotland's charging network accessibility at output-area resolution. The national view displays a high-access corridor through the central belt, with accessibility scores above 0.8 across most of the Glasgow-Edinburgh axis. City-level zooms confirm that Glasgow, Edinburgh, Aberdeen, and Dundee each contain multiple co-located charging sites whose catchment areas overlap, reducing the average distance to the nearest usable charger. Outside these urban clusters, much of the Highlands and island geography falls into lower accessibility bands, where chargers are more widely spaced and fewer alternative sites sit within a short detour. These area diagnostics use geometric OA centroids and the same archived physical-location network as the trip assessment. They describe local provision; the trip calculation separately tests public access within 500 m of the origin OA centroid and generated destination point and pools demand at each required site. Dense urban networks offer more nearby alternatives, but an OA accessibility score does not establish trip-level access or sufficient station capacity.


```{r}

Fill colour shows the accessibility score (red = poor, blue = good; 0.2-1.0) at 70% opacity beneath roads. Yellow circles mark physical locations, sized by reported charging-point count; triangles indicate unreported counts. City panels use 8 km buffers around city centres."
#| out-width: "100%"
```

```{r}
#| label: load-infrastructure-range-data
#| echo: false
#| include: false
#| message: false
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)

# Define all regions and check which have data available
all_regions <- c("Nestrans", "HITRANS", "SPT", "Tactran", "SESTRAN", "SWESTRANS", "ZetTrans")

# Filter to only available regions
infra_available_regions <- all_regions[sapply(all_regions, function(region) {
    json_file <- opath(region, sprintf("%s_comprehensive_summary.json", region))
    file.exists(json_file)
})]

# Load and process data
results <- lapply(infra_available_regions, function(region) {
    json_file <- opath(region, sprintf("%s_comprehensive_summary.json", region))
    data <- fromJSON(json_file)

    data.frame(
        Region = format_region_name(region),
        `Charging Points` = data$data_coverage$charging_locations,
        `Mean Accessibility` = data$infrastructure_analysis$mean_accessibility_score,
        `Poor Access Areas` = data$infrastructure_analysis$poor_access_areas,
        `Poor Access %` = (data$infrastructure_analysis$poor_access_areas / data$data_coverage$demographic_areas) * 100,
        `Short-trip routes %` = data$range_analysis$feasible_routes_pct,
        `Mid-range routes %` = data$range_analysis$constrained_routes_pct,
        `Long-trip routes %` = data$range_analysis$infeasible_routes_pct,
        `Routes` = data$data_coverage$routes,
        check.names = FALSE
    )
}) |> bind_rows()

# Calculate trip-weighted Scotland-wide averages
scotland_feasible_pct <- weighted.mean(results$`Short-trip routes %`, results$Routes, na.rm = TRUE)
scotland_constrained_pct <- weighted.mean(results$`Mid-range routes %`, results$Routes, na.rm = TRUE)
scotland_infeasible_pct <- weighted.mean(results$`Long-trip routes %`, results$Routes, na.rm = TRUE)
```

@tbl-infrastructure-range-summary pairs the spatial accessibility pattern in @fig-charging-infrastructure-map with route-level one-way distance bands at regional level. Scotland-wide, `r sprintf("%.1f%%", scotland_feasible_pct)` of OD routes fall in the short-trip band (<=40 km one-way, round-trip within 80 km effective range), `r sprintf("%.1f%%", scotland_constrained_pct)` fall in the mid-range band (40-80 km one-way, within effective range but requiring destination charging to close a round-trip), and `r sprintf("%.1f%%", scotland_infeasible_pct)` exceed the 80 km effective range one-way. These are route-level distance-only shares: each retained routed record is counted once, and no demographic, home-charging, trip-purpose, or infrastructure-capacity filter has been applied. These unweighted route-level shares describe the spatial network. Volume-weighted distance feasibility can exceed them because short trips carry higher travel volumes under distance decay.
`r format_region_name("SESTRAN")` and `r format_region_name("SPT")` exhibit similarly high mean accessibility (`r sprintf("%.3f", results[results$Region == format_region_name("SESTRAN"), "Mean Accessibility"])`, `r sprintf("%.3f", results[results$Region == format_region_name("SPT"), "Mean Accessibility"])`) and substantial mid-range shares (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", results[results$Region == format_region_name("SESTRAN"), "Mid-range routes %"])`, `r sprintf("%.1f%%", results[results$Region == format_region_name("SPT"), "Mid-range routes %"])` in the 40–80 km band), combining relatively good area-level coverage with a route subset that requires destination charging. These route counts do not measure charging demand.
`r format_region_name("HITRANS")` records lower accessibility (`r sprintf("%.3f", results[results$Region == format_region_name("HITRANS"), "Mean Accessibility"])`), a high poor-access share (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", results[results$Region == format_region_name("HITRANS"), "Poor Access %"])`), and the largest long-trip share (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", results[results$Region == format_region_name("HITRANS"), "Long-trip routes %"])` of routes exceeding 80 km one way), consistent with the Highlands and Islands geography, where dispersed settlements and longer inter-settlement travel distances are associated with wider charger spacing and a greater prevalence of long trips.
`r format_region_name("ZetTrans")` presents a distinct pattern: with a short-trip share of `r sprintf("%.1f%%", results[results$Region == format_region_name("ZetTrans"), "Short-trip routes %"])` (<=40 km), the region records the lowest mean accessibility (`r sprintf("%.3f", results[results$Region == format_region_name("ZetTrans"), "Mean Accessibility"])`), indicating a potential spatial coverage gap. Destination access and station capacity require the separate trip-level checks; low mean OA accessibility alone does not establish either result.

Distance-band shares exclude demographic, home-charging, purpose, and capacity filters; see @tbl-trip-purpose-replacement for the full substitution rate."

### Spatial status of the frugal target market and charging provision

```{r}
#| label: spatial-cluster-summary-inputs
#| echo: false
#| message: false
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

r2_join_oa_accessibility <- function(adoption_data, charging_data, context) {
    r2_validate_oa_scores(
        adoption_data,
        c("final_adoption_propensity", "home_charging_feasibility"), context
    )
    stopifnot(nrow(charging_data) == nrow(adoption_data))
    if ("geo_code" %in% names(charging_data)) {
        r2_validate_oa_scores(charging_data, "accessibility_score", context)
        charging_ids <- as.character(charging_data$geo_code)
        if (!setequal(adoption_data$geo_code, charging_ids)) {
            stop(context, ": charging and canonical OA identities differ")
        }
        charging_row <- match(adoption_data$geo_code, charging_ids)
    } else {
        # Legacy exports may omit geo_code. Accept only a complete one-to-one
        # geometry-equivalent mapping; a nearest/within match cannot establish
        # that the two layers describe the same OA inventory.
        if (!inherits(adoption_data, "sf") || !inherits(charging_data, "sf") ||
            is.na(sf::st_crs(adoption_data)) || is.na(sf::st_crs(charging_data))) {
            stop(context, ": missing identifiers require georeferenced OA geometries")
        }
        charging_geometry <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_geometry(charging_data), sf::st_crs(adoption_data))
        matches <- sf::st_equals(sf::st_geometry(adoption_data), charging_geometry)
        if (any(lengths(matches) != 1L)) {
            stop(context, ": legacy charging geometry has unmatched or ambiguous OAs")
        }
        charging_row <- vapply(matches, function(x) x[[1L]], integer(1))
        if (anyDuplicated(charging_row)) {
            stop(context, ": legacy charging geometry would be reused for multiple OAs")
        }
    }
    joined <- if (inherits(adoption_data, "sf")) sf::st_drop_geometry(adoption_data) else adoption_data
    joined$accessibility_score <- charging_data$accessibility_score[charging_row]
    r2_validate_oa_scores(
        joined,
        c("final_adoption_propensity", "home_charging_feasibility", "accessibility_score"), context
    )
    stopifnot(nrow(joined) == nrow(adoption_data), identical(joined$geo_code, adoption_data$geo_code))
    joined
}

home_charging_cluster_threshold <- 0.5
public_access_cluster_threshold <- 0.6
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(available_regions), setequal(available_regions, names(canonical_oa_by_region)))
cluster_inputs_by_region <- setNames(lapply(available_regions, function(region) {
    # Area diagnostics use the exact frozen OA identities, geometry and AP/HCF scores.
    charging_path <- opath(region, "enhanced_charging_infrastructure.gpkg")
    stopifnot(file.exists(charging_path))
    charging_data <- st_read(charging_path, quiet = TRUE)
    r2_join_oa_accessibility(canonical_oa_by_region[[region]], charging_data, region)
}), available_regions)
cluster_summary_inputs <- bind_rows(cluster_inputs_by_region)
stopifnot(
    nrow(cluster_summary_inputs) == total_oas,
    !anyDuplicated(cluster_summary_inputs$geo_code),
    setequal(cluster_summary_inputs$geo_code, all_adoption_data$geo_code),
    sum(r2_target_band(cluster_summary_inputs$final_adoption_propensity)) == target_band_count
)
scotland_frugal_target_pct <- 100 *
    sum(r2_target_band(cluster_summary_inputs$final_adoption_propensity)) / total_oas
home_charging_cluster_median <- median(cluster_summary_inputs$home_charging_feasibility)
public_access_cluster_q25 <- as.numeric(quantile(
    cluster_summary_inputs$accessibility_score,
    probs = 0.25
))
```

This subsection presents two spatial snapshots of Scotland's charging landscape: an RTP-scale charging-score typology for the frugal EV target market (adoption propensity between `r sprintf("%.1f", frugal_ap_lower)` and `r sprintf("%.1f", frugal_ap_upper)`) in @tbl-spatial-clusters, and the joint distribution of charging accessibility and the local charger-density factor across Output Areas in @fig-infrastructure-accessibility-capacity. The frugal target market captures `r sprintf("%.1f%%", scotland_frugal_target_pct)` of Scotland's Output Areas.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spatial-clusters
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Spatial clustering analysis for the frugal EV target market (adoption propensity 0.3-0.8). 'Frugal Target (% of RTP)' uses all Output Areas in each RTP as the denominator. Both scores met denotes HCF >= 0.5 and public-access score >= 0.6 within the AP target. These are area-level proxy categories, not trip-level operational readiness."
#| message: false
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Calculate spatial cluster statistics for each region
cluster_stats <- list()

for (region in available_regions) {
    merged_data <- cluster_inputs_by_region[[region]]
    n_areas <- nrow(merged_data)
    frugal_target <- r2_target_band(merged_data$final_adoption_propensity)
    high_home_charge <- merged_data$home_charging_feasibility >= home_charging_cluster_threshold
    high_public_access <- merged_data$accessibility_score >= public_access_cluster_threshold

    n_frugal <- sum(frugal_target)
    high_high <- sum(frugal_target & high_home_charge & high_public_access)
    home_gap <- sum(frugal_target & !high_home_charge & high_public_access)
    public_gap <- sum(frugal_target & high_home_charge & !high_public_access)
    dual_gap <- sum(frugal_target & !high_home_charge & !high_public_access)
    expected <- r2_oa_counts[match(region, r2_oa_counts$region), ]
    stopifnot(
        n_areas == expected$total_areas, n_frugal == expected$target_areas,
        high_high + home_gap + public_gap + dual_gap == n_frugal
    )
    cluster_stats[[region]] <- data.frame(
        Region = format_region_name(region),
        `Frugal Target (% of RTP)` = round((n_frugal / n_areas) * 100, 1),
        `Deployment Ready (% of Frugal Target)` = if (n_frugal > 0) round((high_high / n_frugal) * 100, 1) else NA_real_,
        `Home Charging Gap (% of Frugal Target)` = if (n_frugal > 0) round((home_gap / n_frugal) * 100, 1) else NA_real_,
        `Public Access Gap (% of Frugal Target)` = if (n_frugal > 0) round((public_gap / n_frugal) * 100, 1) else NA_real_,
        `Dual Infrastructure Gap (% of Frugal Target)` = if (n_frugal > 0) round((dual_gap / n_frugal) * 100, 1) else NA_real_,
        check.names = FALSE
    )
}
stopifnot(length(cluster_stats) == length(regions))

cluster_table <- bind_rows(cluster_stats)

cluster_display <- cluster_table
if (knitr::is_latex_output() || knitr::is_html_output()) {
    mark_format <- if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "latex" else "html"
    for (col in 2:ncol(cluster_table)) {
        values <- sprintf("%.1f", cluster_table[[col]])
        cluster_display[[col]] <- kableExtra::cell_spec(
            values,
            format = mark_format, color = "black"
        )
    }
}

if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    cluster_col_names <- c(
        "Region",
        linebreak("Frugal target\n(\\% of RTP)"),
        linebreak("Both scores met\n(\\% of Frugal Target)"),
        linebreak("Home charging gap\n(\\% of Frugal Target)"),
        linebreak("Public access gap\n(\\% of Frugal Target)"),
        linebreak("Dual gap\n(\\% of Frugal Target)")
    )

    cluster_kable <- kbl(
        cluster_display,
        format = "latex",
        booktabs = TRUE,
        longtable = TRUE,
        escape = FALSE,
        col.names = cluster_col_names,
        align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
        row.names = FALSE
    ) |>
        kable_styling(font_size = 10, full_width = FALSE) |>
        column_spec(1, width = "2.1cm") |>
        column_spec(2, width = "2.1cm") |>
        column_spec(3, width = "2.5cm") |>
        column_spec(4, width = "2.5cm") |>
        column_spec(5, width = "2.5cm") |>
        column_spec(6, width = "2.3cm")

    # Suppress repeated caption and column headers on continuation pages.
    cluster_kable_str <- sub(
        "\\\\endfirsthead[\\s\\S]*?\\\\endhead",
        "\\\\endfirsthead\n\\\\endhead",
        as.character(cluster_kable),
        perl = TRUE
    )

    class(cluster_kable_str) <- class(cluster_kable)
    attr(cluster_kable_str, "format") <- attr(cluster_kable, "format")
    cluster_kable_str
} else if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    cluster_col_names <- c(
        "Region",
        linebreak("Frugal target\n(% RTP)"),
        linebreak("Both scores met\n(% target)"),
        linebreak("Home charging gap\n(% target)"),
        linebreak("Public access gap\n(% target)"),
        linebreak("Dual gap\n(% target)")
    )

    kbl(
        cluster_display,
        escape = FALSE,
        col.names = cluster_col_names,
        align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
        row.names = FALSE
    ) |>
        kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>

        column_spec(4, width = "9em") |>
        column_spec(5, width = "9em") |>
        column_spec(6, width = "8em")
} else {
    cluster_col_names_plain <- c(
        "Region",
        "Frugal target (% RTP)",
        "Both scores met (% target)",
        "Home charging gap (% target)",
        "Public access gap (% target)",
        "Dual gap (% target)"
    )
    kable(
        cluster_table,
        col.names = cluster_col_names_plain,
        align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),

    )
}
```

@tbl-spatial-clusters reports the frugal-target share per RTP alongside four conditional shares describing how that target population is distributed across charging-score categories, using home-charging feasibility ≥`r sprintf("%.1f", home_charging_cluster_threshold)` and public-access score ≥`r sprintf("%.1f", public_access_cluster_threshold)` as the cluster cut-offs. The frugal-target share ranges from `r sprintf("%.1f%%", lowest_target[['Frugal Target (% of RTP)']])` in `r lowest_target$Region` to `r sprintf("%.1f%%", highest_target[['Frugal Target (% of RTP)']])` in `r highest_target$Region`. Within the frugal target, the share meeting both score thresholds is highest in `r highest_deployment$Region` at `r sprintf("%.1f%%", highest_deployment[['Deployment Ready (% of Frugal Target)']])` and lowest in `r lowest_deployment$Region` at `r sprintf("%.1f%%", lowest_deployment[['Deployment Ready (% of Frugal Target)']])`. The home-charging-gap share exceeds the public-access-gap share in every RTP. Public-access and dual-gap shares remain greatest in the peripheral and island regions. Dual-gap shares remain at or below `r sprintf("%.1f%%", highest_dual_gap[['Dual Infrastructure Gap (% of Frugal Target)']])` across all RTPs, with the highest value in `r highest_dual_gap$Region`.


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# Ensure format_region_name function is available
if (!exists("format_region_name")) {
    format_region_name <- function(region) {

        )

}

# Load charging infrastructure data across regions
infra_scatter_list <- list()
for (region in available_regions) {

    if (file.exists(charging_file)) {
        region_sf <- st_read(charging_file, quiet = TRUE) |>
            st_drop_geometry() |>
            select(geo_code, accessibility_score, capacity_factor, charging_accessibility_category) |>

        infra_scatter_list[[region]] <- region_sf
    }
}

stopifnot(setequal(names(infra_scatter_list), available_regions))
infra_combined <- bind_rows(infra_scatter_list)
stopifnot(
    nrow(infra_combined) == total_oas,
    !anyDuplicated(infra_combined$geo_code),
    setequal(infra_combined$geo_code, all_adoption_data$geo_code)
)
r2_validate_oa_scores(
    infra_combined,
    c("accessibility_score", "capacity_factor"), "National charging diagnostics"
)

# Sample for visualization performance
set.seed(456)
infra_sample <- infra_combined

# Calculate quadrant distribution statistics
adequate <- sum(infra_sample$accessibility_score > 0.7 & infra_sample$capacity_factor > 0.7, na.rm = TRUE)
poor_coverage_high_demand <- sum(infra_sample$accessibility_score <= 0.7 & infra_sample$capacity_factor > 0.7, na.rm = TRUE)
underutilised <- sum(infra_sample$accessibility_score > 0.7 & infra_sample$capacity_factor <= 0.7, na.rm = TRUE)
coverage_gaps <- sum(infra_sample$accessibility_score <= 0.7 & infra_sample$capacity_factor <= 0.7, na.rm = TRUE)
```
@fig-infrastructure-accessibility-capacity plots the charging accessibility score against the area-level capacity factor for Output Areas, coloured by RTP, with reference lines at 0.7 on both axes defining four diagnostic quadrants. These axes represent small-area spatial proxy indices (derived from charger density and proximity within spatial buffers) rather than the physical station charger-hour utilisation (${u_\ell}$, @eq-utilisation) evaluated in the trip-screening model. The lower-right quadrant, with higher proximity scores but lower local charger-density factors, contains `r format(underutilised, big.mark=",")` Output Areas (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", underutilised/nrow(infra_sample)*100)`), indicating that proximity to a single charging location does not necessarily imply high local charger density. The upper-right quadrant, with high scores on both spatial metrics, contains `r format(adequate, big.mark=",")` areas (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", adequate/nrow(infra_sample)*100)`), whilst the lower-left quadrant, with low scores on both metrics, contains `r format(coverage_gaps, big.mark=",")` areas (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", coverage_gaps/nrow(infra_sample)*100)`). The upper-left quadrant is negligible in size. The marginal density distributions show that area-level capacity factors are systematically lower than accessibility scores across RTPs, reflecting the fact that many areas with proximate access have few nearby charging locations rather than a dense group of sites.

```{r}
#| label: fig-infrastructure-accessibility-capacity
#| echo: false

library(ggplot2)

        x = 0.25, y = 0.92,
        label = "Low access\nHigh density",
        color = "orange", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5
    ) +
    annotate("text",
        x = 0.83, y = 0.15,

        color = "purple", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5

# Add marginal density plots
ggMarginal(p_main, type = "density", groupColour = TRUE, groupFill = TRUE, alpha = 0.3)
```

### Constraint decomposition

Five diagnostics describe constraints on the retained local-trip population [@Melliger2018; @Pareschi2020]. @fig-constraint-contribution reports their trip-volume-weighted means and regional dispersion. Absence of home charging affects `r sprintf("%.1f", scotland_constraints$no_home_charging_pct)`\% of raw trip volume, but it is not necessarily binding for short trips with public access. AP outside the target band affects `r sprintf("%.1f", scotland_constraints$demographic_constraint_pct)`\%, and purpose weights below 0.5 apply to `r sprintf("%.1f", scotland_constraints$low_purpose_pct)`\%. The purpose diagnostic is not a binary exclusion. Range beyond 80 km affects `r sprintf("%.2f", scotland_constraints$range_constraint_pct)`\%, partly reflecting the generator's local-distance support. Capacity-constrained theoretical demand is `r sprintf("%.2f", scotland_constraints$insufficient_capacity_pct)`\% of the same denominator, measured after AP, access and purpose weighting. It therefore differs in conditioning from the raw barrier prevalences. These diagnostics overlap and are not additive contributions to a single loss total. Regional variation is descriptive, not evidence of causal effects.

Charging investment has different roles in extending access and relieving capacity deficits. Additional public capacity can serve eligible non-home trips at origin and medium-distance trips at destination, as classified in @eq-trip-classification. Improved home or local public access broadens the demand meeting @eq-feasibility-indicator. The resulting station loads depend on the additional demand served. Average-day capacity remains subject to peak-time queues, reliability, pricing and access restrictions, which affect practical availability.

A further qualification concerns the home-charging barrier specifically. Absent home charging does not bind uniformly across Scotland: it is concentrated in urban flatted neighbourhoods without off-street parking, of which Glasgow, with its large tenement and flatted housing stock, is the clearest Scottish example, whereas detached and semi-detached housing in suburban and rural areas faces minimal installation barriers. The implied priority is therefore not blanket home-charging provision everywhere, but closing the specific gap in flatted, no-parking areas through communal, on-street, and nearby public charging, while home installation proceeds where parking already permits it. In these neighbourhoods the practical delivery mechanism is low-power public charging of around 7 kW integrated into lamp columns or installed at on-street parking bays, which substitutes for the home connection that flatted residents cannot install [@Budnitz2024].

Because Scotland's public charging network is already expanding under existing programmes, the contribution here is not a generic call for more chargers but spatial targeting: identifying, through the constraint geography in @fig-constraint-contribution and the readiness clusters in @tbl-spatial-clusters, where additional provision could support screened trips. That geography maps onto trip-purpose-specific planning actions. For commuting and education trips, which achieve the highest substitution rates (@tbl-trip-purpose-replacement), the long dwell times of vehicles suggest low-power charging as a candidate planning response. For commuting, vehicles typically remain parked for 7–9 hours. Workplace charging can therefore rely on low-power AC connections (3.7–7 kW) that minimise grid connection costs while fully replenishing short-range batteries. For education journeys, a distinction must be made between primary and secondary schools (where brief drop-off dwell times make adjacent charging installations impractical) and higher education campuses, where multi-hour dwell times support low-power destination charging. For park-and-ride facilities, the daily travel pattern implies that installing high-density, low-power chargers allows commuters to leave vehicles charging all day, effectively extending home-charging equivalence to urban residents who lack private off-street parking. For local authority planning, if the objective is to promote frugal EV adoption, the findings identify low-power charging provision in commercial planning consents and public transit interchanges as an option for assessment. Its effectiveness relative to subsidies for rapid-charging hubs is not estimated here. For shopping trips, which typically feature dwell times of 1–2 hours, retail destination charging could use medium-speed AC chargers (7–22 kW) that match visit duration. This is distinct from en-route rapid charging along major highway corridors, which relies on high-power DC chargers (50 kW+) for rapid vehicle turnaround. Because short-range frugal EVs are not designed for long-distance highway transit and often lack DC rapid-charging capabilities, high-power motorway en-route charging does not serve this vehicle class. However, low-to-medium-power destination and service-point charging along rural transit corridors (such as ferry terminals, community hubs, and rural service towns) remains relevant for mid-range rural connectivity. Retail destination charging represents a candidate planning priority to support these local trips; comparative cost-effectiveness relative to other public investments is not evaluated here. For rural and island regions, destination charging at rural service points (such as medical centres, community hubs, and ferry terminals) where vehicles dwell at the trip endpoint can complement home charging at origin for 40--80 km trips requiring public access at the destination, rather than relying on en-route motorway charging. This distinction also marks a mismatch in current charging plans: standard programmes concentrate on high-power rapid-corridor chargers suited to premium, long-range EVs, whereas frugal EVs depend on low-power, extended-dwell residential charging, such as the on-street lamp columns noted above, and on destination charging. Planning can therefore match the charging type to the modelled constraint and dominant trip purpose in each area.

A spatially explicit investment implication follows from reading the adoption-propensity map (@fig-scotland-adoption-propensity) together with this constraint decomposition. Scotland's largest urban cores record relatively low adoption propensity, yet they concentrate the highest volumes of short daily car trips, and for these areas the binding constraint identified above is charging access rather than vehicle range. Where trip density is greatest and charging is the limiting factor, each additional low-power on-street or destination charge point could make feasible a larger absolute number of substitutable trips than the same investment placed in low-demand areas. This identifies high-trip, charging-constrained urban neighbourhoods as candidates for targeted charging assessment. Marginal substitution gains and investment returns require site-specific evaluation.

```{r}
#| label: prep-regional-constraints
#| echo: false
#| include: false
#| message: false
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)

constraint_labels <- c("Range", "Home Chg.", "Capacity", "Purpose", "AP")

regional_constraints <- lapply(infra_available_regions, function(region) {
    json_file <- opath(region, sprintf("%s_comprehensive_summary.json", region))
    data <- fromJSON(json_file)

    vals <- c(
        data$executive_summary$range_constraint_pct,
        data$executive_summary$no_home_charging_pct,
        data$executive_summary$insufficient_capacity_pct,
        data$executive_summary$low_purpose_pct,
        data$executive_summary$demographic_constraint_pct
    )

    data.frame(
        Region = format_region_name(region),
        `Range` = vals[1],
        `Home Chg.` = vals[2],
        `Capacity` = vals[3],
        `Purpose` = vals[4],
        `AP` = vals[5],
        `Dominant` = constraint_labels[which.max(vals)],
        check.names = FALSE
    )
}) |> bind_rows()

# Add Scotland-wide row
scotland_row <- data.frame(
    Region = "Scotland",
    `Range` = scotland_constraints$range_constraint_pct,
    `Home Chg.` = scotland_constraints$no_home_charging_pct,
    `Capacity` = scotland_constraints$insufficient_capacity_pct,
    `Purpose` = scotland_constraints$low_purpose_pct,
    `AP` = scotland_constraints$demographic_constraint_pct,
    `Dominant` = constraint_labels[which.max(c(
        scotland_constraints$range_constraint_pct,
        scotland_constraints$no_home_charging_pct,
        scotland_constraints$insufficient_capacity_pct,
        scotland_constraints$low_purpose_pct,
        scotland_constraints$demographic_constraint_pct
    ))],
    check.names = FALSE
)

regional_constraints <- bind_rows(regional_constraints, scotland_row)
```



```{r}
#| label: fig-constraint-contribution
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Constraint contribution analysis across five barrier dimensions and three enabler dimensions. Left panel: trip-volume-weighted mean prevalence with min-max error bars across seven regions. Right panel: coefficient of variation quantifying regional dispersion. Stars retain exploratory one-sample tests of the unweighted regional means against zero (*** p<0.001, ** p<0.01, * p<0.05); these do not test regional variation or causal effects."
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 10
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)

# Extract constraint metrics from regional data with safe extraction
safe_numeric <- function(val, default = 0) {
    if (is.null(val) || length(val) == 0 || is.na(val)) {
        return(default)
    }
    as.numeric(val)
}

constraint_metrics <- data.frame(
    Region = available_regions,
    Range_Constraint = sapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) {
        tryCatch(safe_numeric(x$executive_summary$range_constraint_pct, 0), error = function(e) 0)
    }),
    No_Home_Charging = sapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) {
        tryCatch(safe_numeric(x$executive_summary$no_home_charging_pct, 0), error = function(e) 0)
    }),
    Insufficient_Capacity = sapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) {
        tryCatch(safe_numeric(x$executive_summary$insufficient_capacity_pct, 0), error = function(e) 0)
    }),
    Low_Purpose = sapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) {
        tryCatch(safe_numeric(x$executive_summary$low_purpose_pct, 0), error = function(e) 0)
    }),
    Demographic_Constraint = sapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) {
        tryCatch(safe_numeric(x$executive_summary$demographic_constraint_pct, 0), error = function(e) 0)
    }),
    Adoption_Propensity = sapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) {
        tryCatch(
            {
                # Try adoption_analysis first, then adoption_propensity
                val <- x$adoption_analysis$mean_adoption_propensity
                if (is.null(val) || length(val) == 0) {
                    val <- x$adoption_propensity$mean_adoption_propensity
                }
                safe_numeric(val, 0)
            },
            error = function(e) 0
        )
    }),
    Home_Charging = sapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) {
        tryCatch(
            {
                # Try adoption_analysis first, then adoption_propensity
                val <- x$adoption_analysis$mean_home_charging_feasibility
                if (is.null(val) || length(val) == 0) {
                    val <- x$adoption_propensity$mean_home_charging_feasibility
                }
                safe_numeric(val, 0)
            },
            error = function(e) 0
        )
    }),
    Infrastructure_Access = sapply(regional_data[available_regions], function(x) {
        tryCatch(safe_numeric(x$infrastructure_analysis$mean_accessibility_score, 0), error = function(e) 0)
    })
)

# Calculate statistics
constraint_summary <- constraint_metrics |>
    summarise(
        across(Range_Constraint:Infrastructure_Access,
            list(
                mean = ~ weighted.mean(., trip_weights, na.rm = TRUE),
                min = ~ min(., na.rm = TRUE),
                max = ~ max(., na.rm = TRUE),
                sd = ~ sd(., na.rm = TRUE)
            ),
            .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
        )
    )

# Retain exploratory zero-mean tests; these do not test regional variation.
sig_tests <- data.frame(
    Constraint = c(
        "Range Limitation", "No Home Charging", "Insufficient Capacity",
        "Low Purpose Suitability", "AP Outside Range",
        "Adoption Propensity", "Home Charging Feasibility", "Infrastructure Accessibility"
    ),
    p_value = c(
        t.test(constraint_metrics$Range_Constraint)$p.value,
        t.test(constraint_metrics$No_Home_Charging)$p.value,
        t.test(constraint_metrics$Insufficient_Capacity)$p.value,
        t.test(constraint_metrics$Low_Purpose)$p.value,
        t.test(constraint_metrics$Demographic_Constraint)$p.value,
        t.test(constraint_metrics$Adoption_Propensity)$p.value,
        t.test(constraint_metrics$Home_Charging)$p.value,
        t.test(constraint_metrics$Infrastructure_Access)$p.value
    )
)

sig_tests$significance <- ifelse(sig_tests$p_value < 0.001, "***",
    ifelse(sig_tests$p_value < 0.01, "**",
        ifelse(sig_tests$p_value < 0.05, "*", "")
    )
)

# Panel A: Community-weighted constraint means (5 barriers)
panel_a_data <- data.frame(
    Constraint = c(
        "Range\nLimitation", "No Home\nCharging", "Insufficient\nCapacity",
        "Low Purpose\nSuitability", "AP Outside\nRange"
    ),
    Mean_Impact = c(
        constraint_summary$Range_Constraint_mean,
        constraint_summary$No_Home_Charging_mean,
        constraint_summary$Insufficient_Capacity_mean,
        constraint_summary$Low_Purpose_mean,
        constraint_summary$Demographic_Constraint_mean
    ),
    Min = c(
        constraint_summary$Range_Constraint_min,
        constraint_summary$No_Home_Charging_min,
        constraint_summary$Insufficient_Capacity_min,
        constraint_summary$Low_Purpose_min,
        constraint_summary$Demographic_Constraint_min
    ),
    Max = c(
        constraint_summary$Range_Constraint_max,
        constraint_summary$No_Home_Charging_max,
        constraint_summary$Insufficient_Capacity_max,
        constraint_summary$Low_Purpose_max,
        constraint_summary$Demographic_Constraint_max
    ),
    Type = "Barrier",
    Significance = sig_tests$significance[1:5]
)

panel_a_data_b <- data.frame(
    Constraint = c("Adoption\nPropensity", "Home Charging\nFeasibility", "Infrastructure\nAccessibility"),
    Mean_Impact = c(
        constraint_summary$Adoption_Propensity_mean * 100,
        constraint_summary$Home_Charging_mean * 100,
        constraint_summary$Infrastructure_Access_mean * 100
    ),
    Min = c(
        constraint_summary$Adoption_Propensity_min * 100,
        constraint_summary$Home_Charging_min * 100,
        constraint_summary$Infrastructure_Access_min * 100
    ),
    Max = c(
        constraint_summary$Adoption_Propensity_max * 100,
        constraint_summary$Home_Charging_max * 100,
        constraint_summary$Infrastructure_Access_max * 100
    ),
    Type = "Enabler",
    Significance = sig_tests$significance[6:8]
)

panel_a_combined <- bind_rows(panel_a_data, panel_a_data_b)
panel_a_combined$Constraint <- factor(panel_a_combined$Constraint,
    levels = rev(panel_a_combined$Constraint)
)

pad_a <- max(panel_a_combined$Max - panel_a_combined$Min, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.08
pad_a <- ifelse(is.finite(pad_a) && pad_a > 0, pad_a, 3)

xmax_a <- max(panel_a_combined$Max, na.rm = TRUE) + 4 * pad_a

# Panel A: Community-weighted constraint means
p1 <- ggplot(panel_a_combined, aes(x = Mean_Impact, y = Constraint, fill = Type)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, alpha = 0.9) +
    geom_errorbarh(
        aes(xmin = Min, xmax = Max),
        height = 0.25, linewidth = 0.7, color = "gray25"
    ) +
    # significance stars just outside the errorbar
    geom_text(
        aes(x = Max + 0.5 * pad_a, label = Significance),
        hjust = 0, size = 5, fontface = "bold", color = "black"
    ) +
    # value labels further right, after the stars
    geom_label(
        aes(x = Max + 2.0 * pad_a, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", Mean_Impact)),
        hjust = 0, size = 4.2, fontface = "bold",
        label.size = 0, fill = "white", label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines")
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Barrier" = "#DC143C", "Enabler" = "#2E8B57")) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        limits = c(0, xmax_a),
        expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Trip-Volume-Weighted Constraint Diagnostics",
        x = "Trip-Volume-Weighted Impact (%)",
        y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, margin = margin(b = 8)),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(t = 8)),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
        plot.margin = margin(12, 16, 12, 12)
    )

# ---- Panel B: Regional dispersion (CV%) ----
panel_b_barriers <- data.frame(
    Constraint = c(
        "Range\nLimitation", "No Home\nCharging", "Insufficient\nCapacity",
        "Low Purpose\nSuitability", "AP Outside\nRange"
    ),
    CV = c(
        ifelse(constraint_summary$Range_Constraint_mean > 0,
            constraint_summary$Range_Constraint_sd / constraint_summary$Range_Constraint_mean * 100, 0
        ),
        ifelse(constraint_summary$No_Home_Charging_mean > 0,
            constraint_summary$No_Home_Charging_sd / constraint_summary$No_Home_Charging_mean * 100, 0
        ),
        ifelse(constraint_summary$Insufficient_Capacity_mean > 0,
            constraint_summary$Insufficient_Capacity_sd / constraint_summary$Insufficient_Capacity_mean * 100, 0
        ),
        ifelse(constraint_summary$Low_Purpose_mean > 0,
            constraint_summary$Low_Purpose_sd / constraint_summary$Low_Purpose_mean * 100, 0
        ),
        ifelse(constraint_summary$Demographic_Constraint_mean > 0,
            constraint_summary$Demographic_Constraint_sd / constraint_summary$Demographic_Constraint_mean * 100, 0
        )
    ),
    Type = "Barrier",
    Significance = sig_tests$significance[1:5]
)

panel_b_enablers <- data.frame(
    Constraint = c("Adoption\nPropensity", "Home Charging\nFeasibility", "Infrastructure\nAccessibility"),
    CV = c(
        ifelse(constraint_summary$Adoption_Propensity_mean > 0,
            constraint_summary$Adoption_Propensity_sd / constraint_summary$Adoption_Propensity_mean * 100, 0
        ),
        ifelse(constraint_summary$Home_Charging_mean > 0,
            constraint_summary$Home_Charging_sd / constraint_summary$Home_Charging_mean * 100, 0
        ),
        ifelse(constraint_summary$Infrastructure_Access_mean > 0,
            constraint_summary$Infrastructure_Access_sd / constraint_summary$Infrastructure_Access_mean * 100, 0
        )
    ),
    Type = "Enabler",
    Significance = sig_tests$significance[6:8]
)

panel_b_data <- bind_rows(panel_b_barriers, panel_b_enablers)
panel_b_data$Constraint <- factor(panel_b_data$Constraint,
    levels = rev(panel_b_data$Constraint)
)

pad_b <- max(panel_b_data$CV, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.03
pad_b <- ifelse(is.finite(pad_b) && pad_b > 0, pad_b, 5)

xmax_b <- max(panel_b_data$CV, na.rm = TRUE) + 6 * pad_b

p2 <- ggplot(panel_b_data, aes(x = CV, y = Constraint, fill = Type)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, alpha = 0.9) +
    geom_text(
        aes(x = CV + 0.5 * pad_b, label = Significance),

    geom_label(
        aes(x = CV + 2.0 * pad_b, label = sprintf("%.1f", CV)),
``` 

# Limitations and Future Directions {#sec-limitations}

The trip denominator comprises retained synthetic local car-person trips generated under the 40 km candidate-search setting and subsequent distance filtering. The reported suitability shares therefore do not estimate the share of all Scottish car travel that could be served by frugal EVs.

Five methodological limitations qualify the reported feasibility shares. First, trips are analysed independently rather than as complete daily tours. Accumulated distance across a commute, escort leg and shopping stop may exceed the effective range even when each leg is individually feasible. The loss-budget analysis in [Appendix B.6](#sec-chaining-sensitivity) applies only to the home-chargeable, short-trip subset, for which the minimum of `r sprintf("%.1f", r2_chain_floor)`\% is conditional on holding all other trips fixed and is not a national lower bound. The tour diagnostic excludes en-route and destination recharging. For fixed routes and usable battery range, this is conservative with respect to charging opportunities: feasible intermediate recharging could reduce range failures. Second, trip suitability does not establish adoption: a household may retain a larger vehicle for occasional needs despite predominantly short daily trips. No independent held-out sample of frugal-EV uptake or realised substitutions is available.

Three further limitations should be noted. First, infrastructure representation is static and does not capture planned deployment. Second, the charging assessment uses a 0.5 km public-access threshold and evaluates capacity against average daily demand rather than peak-period queuing, so spatial accessibility may overstate practical availability. Third, demographic weighting embeds contestable assumptions: the C2 (skilled manual) weight of 0.25 may undervalue regions where skilled manual workers earn above-average incomes, as in Shetland's fishing and oil economy, and car ownership is treated as a positive adoption indicator (20% weight) despite high rural ownership reflecting transport necessity rather than discretionary choice, a distinction range-feasibility and density adjustments partially mitigate. 

Six extensions address these limitations directly. Individual-level microsimulation would resolve journey complexity and ecological inference, reconstructing daily tours so that chained sequences are evaluated against range as a whole rather than leg by leg. Conditioning the analysis on the existing fleet-segment mix, so that feasible substitution is assessed relative to trips currently served by small and low-cost vehicles rather than the whole car fleet, would move the estimate closer to a vehicle-replacement rather than a trip-suitability quantity. Behavioural integration quantifying range anxiety, technology acceptance, and social influence could support estimates of realised uptake. Economic assessment integrating total cost of ownership would extend the analysis from feasibility to affordability. Uncertainty-aware modelling propagating energy-consumption variation into probabilistic feasibility distributions would quantify confidence around point estimates. Alternative range scenarios (150 km, 200 km) would quantify how extended capacity shifts the feasibility frontier.

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

This study addresses one overarching objective, pursued through three sub-questions, regarding frugal EV deployment across Scotland's 46,359 Output Areas and `r sprintf("%.2f", scotland_totals$total_baseline_trips/1e6)` million retained local daily car-person trips. The framework estimates `r sprintf("%.2f", scotland_totals$total_conversion_potential/1e6)` million access-qualified, purpose-weighted potential car-person trips per day, corresponding to `r sprintf("%.1f", scotland_totals$conversion_rate_pct)`\% of retained baseline demand in the reference scenario. Of this baseline demand, `r r2_pct(r2_metrics$immediate_volume)`\% also satisfies the assumed public-capacity requirements. Across separate AP-band, distance-decay and purpose-weight scenarios, theoretical shares range from `r sprintf("%.1f", r2_envelope[1])`\% to `r sprintf("%.1f", r2_envelope[2])`\% and capacity-sufficient shares from `r sprintf("%.1f", min(r2_scenario_totals$immediate_pct))`\% to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(r2_scenario_totals$immediate_pct))`\%. These are conditional screening results for retained synthetic local trips, not predictions of adoption or vehicle replacement. Methodologically, the study integrates sequential feasibility logic, demographic propensity, purpose-specific suitability and infrastructure assessment. Sensitivity diagnostics and reused BEV benchmarks characterise assumptions and associations. They do not independently validate substitution.

**RQ1: Where and for whom are frugal EVs viable** Analysis identifies `r sprintf("%.1f", scotland_totals$conversion_rate_pct)`% theoretical potential among retained local trips for 100 km nominal-range vehicles, before the separate capacity check, concentrated in suburban areas with moderate adoption propensity (0.3–0.8) and adequate home charging. Where off-street parking exists, supporting home charging installation within this target range is the most tractable lever; in flatted urban areas without off-street parking, where home charging is largely infeasible, public and communal charging solutions are required to extend equitable access. Both pathways are framed as conditional levers expected to raise modelled feasibility rather than guarantees of uptake.

**RQ2: Which trip purposes are most suitable** High-suitability purposes (`r top3$purpose[1]` `r sprintf("%.1f", top3$rate[1])`%, `r top3$purpose[2]` `r sprintf("%.1f", top3$rate[2])`%, `r top3$purpose[3]` `r sprintf("%.1f", top3$rate[3])`%) achieve substitution rates ~`r sprintf("%.0f", high_vs_low_pct)`% higher than low-suitability purposes (`r low2$purpose[1]` `r sprintf("%.1f", low2$rate[1])`%, `r low2$purpose[2]` `r sprintf("%.1f", low2$rate[2])`%), consistent with the trip-purpose heterogeneity in EV user experience documented in the literature [@DaramyWilliams2019UserExperience]. Infrastructure priorities should target workplace charging for commuting and destination charging at retail centres.

**RQ3: What infrastructure gaps constrain modelled substitution suitability?** Public-capacity shortfalls at required trip endpoints account for `r sprintf("%.1f", scotland_totals$constrained_pct)`% of total retained daily car-person-trip volume after purpose weighting and the AP, range and access gates. Origin public capacity is required where home charging is unavailable, while destination capacity is required for trips of 40–80 km. These results identify capacity limitations among otherwise eligible trips and provide a basis for assessing additional charging capacity at the affected endpoints.

The principal conclusion is that the estimated potential depends materially on the market screen and purpose weighting, even where most generated local trips satisfy the distance limit. Charging access determines eligibility, while the separate average-day capacity assessment identifies a smaller constrained part of the theoretical total. The framework locates where, and for which purposes, scenario-qualified suitability is concentrated so that screening can precede investment. Transferability requires the same caution: comparable census, OD and charging data permit application elsewhere, but demographic scores, charging assumptions, purpose weights and the resulting shares require local assessment.

# Appendix A: Extended Methodology Specifications {#app-extended-methodology .unnumbered}

This appendix provides the complete sub-component equations underlying the eight-stage framework. The main text presents each stage's governing equations and interpretive rationale; this appendix supplies the detailed parameterisation (scoring rubrics, interaction thresholds, normalisation rules) required for independent replication. Readers seeking to understand model behaviour should consult the main text; readers seeking to reproduce or extend the implementation should consult the specifications below.

**2011-to-2022 Census Compatibility Layer.** Demographic inputs were migrated from Scotland's 2011 Census to the 2022 Census (National Records of Scotland, released March 2025). A compatibility layer maps 2022 variable codes to the eight scoring domains. Three methodological caveats apply. (i) Social grade is operationalised via NS-SeC (MV609); full-time students (L15) are assigned to the C1 proxy band, which may slightly inflate C1 scores in university-heavy Output Areas. (ii) The age variable MV104 ("aged 65 and over") covers individuals aged 66 and above in the 2022 release, introducing a one-year boundary shift relative to the 2011 equivalent. (iii) The 2022 household-composition variable collapses the married/cohabiting distinction present in 2011, reducing granularity in the household-type component. The study inventory comprises 46,359 OAs in the 2022 geography.

## A.1 OD Disaggregation {#sec-od-disaggregation-appendix .unnumbered}

Zone-to-zone OD flows are transformed into point-to-point desire lines through gravity-model principles.

**Trip Generation:**

$$
{T_{all,i}^{(p)} = P_i \cdot R_{base} \cdot \phi_p \cdot \delta_p}
$$ {#eq-trip-generation-all-mode-app}

$$
{T_{i}^{(p)} = T_{all,i}^{(p)} \cdot m_{car}}
$$ {#eq-trip-generation-app}

where ${T_{all,i}^{(p)}}$ represents all-mode daily person trips from zone $i$ for purpose $p$, $P_i$ denotes population, $R_{base} = 2.61$ is the baseline all-mode trip rate [@NTS2020], $\phi_p$ captures purpose-specific proportions [@SHS2019], and $\delta_p$ represents the included distance-frequency share. Car-person trip production ${T_i^{(p)}}$ applies the Scottish car-mode share ${m_{car} = 0.652}$ (comprising driver and passenger journeys from the Scottish Household Survey [@SHS2019]), which defines the pool of routine car travel evaluated for frugal-EV substitution. The implemented generator uses a 40 km candidate-search setting, followed by a 0.5--40 km jittered-distance filter. Network distances may exceed 40 km. All successfully routed trips are retained. The resulting denominator therefore describes the generated local-trip population, not every Scottish car journey.

**Destination Attractiveness:**

$$
A_j^{(p)} = \sum_{k \in G_j} w_k^{(p)}
$$ {#eq-destination-attractiveness-app}

where $A_j^{(p)}$ represents the attractiveness of grid point $j$ for purpose $p$, $G_j$ denotes the set of POIs assigned to grid point $j$, and $w_k^{(p)} = 1$ for all POI types.

**Gravity Model:**

$$
T_{ij}^{(p)} = \frac{T_i^{(p)} \cdot A_j^{(p)} \cdot \exp\left(\beta_p\frac{d_{ij}^{E}}{1000}\right)}{\sum_k A_k^{(p)} \cdot \exp\left(\beta_p\frac{d_{ik}^{E}}{1000}\right)}
$$ {#eq-gravity-model-app}

where $T_{ij}^{(p)}$ represents trips between origin $i$ and destination $j$ for purpose $p$, $T_i^{(p)}$ denotes origin trip production, $d_{ij}^{E}$ denotes pre-jitter straight-line geographic distance approximation in metres, and $\beta_p<0$ is the signed distance-decay coefficient in km$^{-1}$. Division by 1,000 converts metres to kilometres, so the exponential weight decreases with distance. The NTS-informed coefficient file supplies the following values, read directly during document compilation: $\beta_{commute} = `r r2_beta("Commuting")`$, $\beta_{shop} = `r r2_beta("Shopping")`$, $\beta_{social} = `r r2_beta("Social")`$, and $\beta_{leisure} = `r r2_beta("Leisure")`$ km$^{-1}$. Commuting, business, education, and escort use the commuting profile. Health visits, personal business, and other journeys use the shopping profile. Visiting friends and relatives use the social profile. Eating/drinking, sport, and holidays use the leisure profile.

**Computational Filtering:**

$$
n_{dest,i} = \text{round}\left(\frac{T_i^{(p)}}{\min(T^{(p)})} \cdot 5\right)
$$ {#eq-destination-filtering-app}

where $n_{dest,i}$ is the destination sample size for origin $i$ and purpose $p$, scaled relative to the minimum origin trip production $\min(T^{(p)})$ and capped by the candidates returned by a 40 km nearest-neighbour search. The implementation recomputes distance between the geographic coordinates using the Mapbox cheap-ruler approximation (metres), without refiltering that distance against 40 km; pre-jitter gravity distances therefore extend slightly beyond 40 km. After point jittering, straight-line lengths must satisfy $0.5<d<40$ km before routing. Destinations are sampled without replacement using interaction weights, and retained weights are renormalised to preserve each origin's production before jittering.

**Point-to-Point Conversion:**

$$
f_{ab}^{(p)} = T_{ij}^{(p)} \cdot \frac{\alpha_{ia} \cdot \gamma_{jb}}{\sum_{a' \in \mathcal{A}_i} \sum_{b' \in \mathcal{B}_j} \alpha_{ia'} \cdot \gamma_{jb'}}
$$ {#eq-point-to-point-app}

where $f_{ab}^{(p)}$ represents disaggregated flow between origin anchor point $a \in \mathcal{A}_i$ (Output Area population centroid) and destination point $b \in \mathcal{B}_j$ (POI or residential centroid), with origin and destination allocation weights $\alpha_{ia}$ and $\gamma_{jb}$.

## A.2 Demographic Scoring Components {#sec-demographic-scoring-appendix .unnumbered}

The composite demographic score integrates component scores with these specifications.

**Social Grade Scoring:**

$$
SG_i = \frac{AB_i \cdot 1.0 + C1_i \cdot 0.65 + C2_i \cdot 0.25 + DE_i \cdot 0.0}{AB_i + C1_i + C2_i + DE_i}
$$ {#eq-social-grade-app}

where $AB_i$, $C1_i$, $C2_i$, $DE_i$ represent people in the 2022 NS-SeC-by-tenure table mapped to social-grade proxies, not household counts or directly observed 2011 social grades. AB combines L1–L3. C1 combines L4–L7 and full-time students (L15). C2 combines L8–L11. DE combines L12–L14. This compatibility mapping, including the student allocation, is an assumption.

**Education Scoring:**

$$
ED_i = \frac{L4_i \cdot 1.0 + L3_i \cdot 0.75 + L2_i \cdot 0.35 + L1_i \cdot 0.10 + NQ_i \cdot 0.0}{L4_i + L3_i + L2_i + L1_i + NQ_i}
$$ {#eq-education-score-app}

where $L4_i$ through $NQ_i$ represent people aged 16 and over by qualification level.

**Car Ownership Scoring:**

$$
CO_i = \frac{NC_i \cdot 0.0 + OC_i \cdot 0.4 + TC_i \cdot 1.0}{NC_i + OC_i + TC_i}
$$ {#eq-car-ownership-app}

where $NC_i$, $OC_i$, $TC_i$ denote households with no cars, one car, and two+ cars respectively.

**Housing Scoring:**

$$
HT_i = \frac{HB_i \cdot 1.0 + FA_i \cdot 0.15}{HB_i + FA_i}
$$ {#eq-housing-score-app}

where $HB_i$ and $FA_i$ represent houses/bungalows and flats/apartments respectively.

## A.3 Home Charging Feasibility Components {#sec-home-charging-feasibility-appendix .unnumbered}

**Accommodation Feasibility:**

$$
F_{acc,i} = \frac{w_{h,acc} \cdot H_{car,i} + w_{f,acc} \cdot F_{car,i} + w_{o,acc} \cdot O_{car,i}}{H_{car,i} + F_{car,i} + O_{car,i}}
$$ {#eq-accommodation-feasibility-app}

where $H_{car,i}$, $F_{car,i}$, $O_{car,i}$ represent car-owning households in houses, flats, and other accommodation, with weights $w_{h,acc} = 0.92$, $w_{f,acc} = 0.22$, $w_{o,acc} = 0.50$ representing assumed relative charging suitability rather than fitted Scottish installation rates [@Nicholas2020].

**Parking Availability Inference:**

$$
M_i = \min\left(1.0 + 0.3 \cdot \frac{TC_i}{TH_i}, 1.3\right)
$$ {#eq-parking-multiplier-app}

$$
\mathcal{P}_i = \min\left(1, \max\left(0, \frac{M_i - M_{\min}}{M_{\max} - M_{\min} + \varepsilon}\right)\right)
$$ {#eq-parking-score-app}

where $TC_i$ represents households with two+ vehicles, $TH_i$ denotes total households, and $M_i$ ranges from 1.0 to 1.3. The rescaling uses fixed anchors $M_{{\min}}\mathrel{=}{1.0}$ and ${M}_{{\max}}\mathrel{=}{1.3}$, so $\mathcal{{P}}_{i}$ is numerically the multi-car-household fraction, used as a proxy for parking access.

**Home Charging Feasibility:**

$$
{HCF_i = w_a \cdot F_{acc,i} + w_p \cdot \mathcal{P}_i}
$$ {#eq-home-charging-feasibility-raw-app}

[]{#eq-hcf-normalized-app}

where $w_a = 0.2$ and $w_p = 0.8$ represent accommodation and parking component weights. Because ${F_{acc,i} \in [0,1]}$ and ${\mathcal{P}_i \in [0,1]}$, their convex combination directly yields a bounded score ${HCF_i \in [0,1]}$. No empirical division by the sample maximum is applied, preserving the absolute interpretation of the ${\tau_{HCF} = 0.5}$ threshold across Output Areas.

## A.4 Demographic Interaction Effects {#sec-demographic-interactions-appendix .unnumbered}

**Income-Education Synergy:**

$$
IE_i = \begin{cases}
1.60 & \text{if } SG_i > 0.7 \text{ and } ED_i > 0.7 \text{ (high synergy)} \\
0.70 & \text{if } SG_i > 0.7 \text{ and } ED_i < 0.4 \text{ (income penalty)} \\
0.70 & \text{if } SG_i < 0.4 \text{ and } ED_i > 0.7 \text{ (education penalty)} \\
0.50 & \text{if } SG_i < 0.4 \text{ and } ED_i < 0.4 \text{ (compound penalty)} \\
1.0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-income-education-multiplier-app}

The piecewise multipliers are modelling assumptions for the joint effects of social grade and education. Appendix B.3 distinguishes these assumptions from the interactions estimated in the cited literature.

**Age-Income Interaction:**

$$
AI_i = \begin{cases}
1.45 & \text{if } {q}_{30{:}44{,}{i}}\mathrel{>}{0.3} \text{ and } SG_i > 0.7 \\
0.55 & \text{if } {q}_{20{:}29{,}{i}}\mathrel{>}{0.3} \text{ and } SG_i < 0.4 \\
0.35 & \text{if } {q}_{65+{,}{i}}\mathrel{>}{0.3} \text{ {and} } {SG}_{i} \mathrel{>} {0.7} \\
1.0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-age-income-multiplier-app}

Survey evidence confirms stark generational differences, with older UK drivers (55+) exhibiting consistently higher reluctance toward EV adoption due to cost concerns and charging infrastructure confidence [@AA2024; @AA2017]. In the piecewise implementation, ${q}_{{a}{,}{i}}$ denotes the population share in age group ${a}$. The stated rules are applied in their displayed order.

**Multi-Car Multiplier:**

$$
MC_i = \begin{cases}
1.55 & \text{if } q_{MC,i} > 0.50 \text{ (high multi-car prevalence)} \\
1.30 & \text{if } 0.30 < q_{MC,i} \leq 0.50 \text{ (moderate multi-car prevalence)} \\
1.00 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-multi-car-multiplier-app}

where $q_{MC,i}=TC_i/(NC_i+OC_i+TC_i)$ is the multi-car-household proportion from the same car-availability table used for $CO_i$. Here $NC_i$, $OC_i$ and $TC_i$ remain household counts [@scotlandcensus2022].

**Interaction-Adjusted Score:**

$$
S_{demo,i}' = S_{demo,i} \cdot IE_i \cdot MC_i \cdot AI_i
$$ {#eq-interaction-adjusted-app}

**Population Density Effects:**

$$  
PD_i = \begin{cases}
0.70 & \text{if } \rho < 10 \text{ people/km}^2 \text{ (remote penalty)} \\
0.75 & \text{if } 10 \leq \rho < 20 \text{ (very rural)} \\
0.85 & \text{if } 20 \leq \rho < 50 \text{ (rural)} \\
1.08 & \text{if } 200 \leq \rho \leq 1000 \text{ (suburban bonus)} \\
0.92 & \text{if } \rho > 2000 \text{ and } FR_i > 0.7 \text{ (high-density high-flat)} \\
0.98 & \text{if } \rho > 2000 \text{ and } FR_i \leq 0.7 \\
1.0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-density-multiplier-app}

where $\rho$ denotes population density (people/km²) and $FR_i$ represents flat ratio [@CMA2021].

**Geographic-Adjusted Score:**

$$
S_{demo,i}'' = \min\left(1.0, \max\left(0.0, S_{demo,i}' \cdot PD_i\right)\right)
$$ {#eq-geographic-adjusted-app}

## A.5 Trip Purpose Charging Flexibility {#sec-trip-purpose-charging-flexibility-appendix .unnumbered}

**Charging Flexibility Score:**

$$
CF_p = w_{dwell} \cdot D_p + w_{timing} \cdot (1 - S_p) + w_{dest} \cdot I_p + w_{home} \cdot (HCF_p)
$$ {#eq-charging-flexibility-app}

where $D_p$ denotes dwell time flexibility, $S_p$ indicates temporal sensitivity, $I_p$ represents destination infrastructure availability, and weights $w_{dwell} = 0.40$, $w_{timing} = 0.30$, $w_{dest} = 0.20$, $w_{home} = 0.10$ [@Hardman2018; @Franke2013]. $I_p$ and $HCF_p$ are fixed purpose-specific ratings, whereas actual OA home charging and station access enter the separate binary gates.

**Binary Home Charging:**

$$
H_i = \mathbf{1}\{HCF_i \geq \tau_{HCF}\}, \quad \tau_{HCF} = 0.5
$$ {#eq-home-charging-binary-app}

## A.6 Charging Infrastructure Analysis {#sec-charging-infrastructure-analysis-appendix .unnumbered}

**Public Charging at Origin:**

$$
\Pi_i = \mathbf{1}\{d_i \leq 0.5 \text{ km}\}
$$ {#eq-public-charging-origin-app}

**Public Charging at Destination:**

$$
\Pi_j = \mathbf{1}\{d_j \leq 0.5 \text{ km}\}
$$ {#eq-public-charging-destination-app}

where the walking distance threshold reflects evidence from user preference research [@Budnitz2024; @Potoglou2023], which documents significant sensitivity to access distance in public charging contexts and supports sub-kilometre proximity as the threshold for viable non-home charging access.

**Public Charging Reliance:**

$$
\rho_i = \min\left(1, B_i + 0.3 \cdot \min\left(1, \frac{d_i}{5}\right)\right)
$$ {#eq-charging-reliance-app}

**Baseline Housing-Based Reliance:**

$$
B_i = \alpha + (\beta - \alpha) \cdot \left(\frac{w_{f,rel} \cdot FA_i}{w_{h,rel} \cdot HB_i + w_{f,rel} \cdot FA_i + \gamma}\right)^\delta
$$ {#eq-baseline-reliance-app}

where $w_{f,rel} = 0.8$ and $w_{h,rel} = 0.2$ reflect charging dependency weights, $\alpha = 0.1$ and $\beta = 0.9$ set bounds.

**Charging Point Density:**

$$
N_R(i) = \sum_j \mathbf{1}\{\lVert r_i - c_j \rVert \leq R\}, \quad R \in \{1000, 2000, 5000\} \text{ metres}
$$ {#eq-charging-density-app}

**Gap Severity:**

$$
G_i = \frac{d_{nearest,i}}{d_{threshold}} \cdot \rho_i \cdot \frac{S_{adoption,i}}{S_{max}}
$$ {#eq-gap-severity-app}

**Energy Required:**

$$
E_{ij} = d_{ij} \cdot \eta_{type}
$$ {#eq-energy-required-app}

| Vehicle Type | Consumption $\eta$ (kWh/km) | Battery (kWh) |
|--------------|------------------------------|---------------|
| 2-seater (CM1) | 0.060 | 7 |
| 4-seater (CM2) | 0.065 | 11 |
: Representative vehicle energy parameters. The capacity calculation uses 0.065 kWh/km for both classes in @eq-energy-consumption. {#tbl-energy-params}

**Charging Time:**

$$
t_{ij} = \frac{E_{ij}}{P_{charge}}
$$ {#eq-charging-time-energy-app}

where $P_{charge} = 7$ kW represents typical public AC charger power.

**Daily Session Capacity:**

$$
C_{daily,{\ell}}={n}_{\ell} T_{op}{/}t_{session}{,}\qquad {T}_{{op}}\mathrel{=}{16}\text{ {h}}{,}\quad {t}_{{session}}\mathrel{=}{2}\text{ {h}}{.}
$$ {#eq-daily-capacity-app}

where $C_{daily,{\ell}}$ represents theoretical daily capacity, ${n}_{\ell}$ denotes charging points, $T_{op} = 16$ hours represents daily operational period, and $t_{session} = 2$ hours indicates average session duration.

**Utilisation Rate Estimation:**

$$
U_\ell^{bg}=\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}\left[
0.45\left(1+0.7\frac{n_\ell-1}{n_\ell-1+b}\right)+\epsilon_\ell\right],
\quad b=0.8\operatorname{median}(n_\ell).
$$ {#eq-utilisation-rate-app}

The utilisation model uses $\epsilon_\ell\sim\mathcal{N}(0,0.08^2/\sqrt{n_\ell})$, generated with seed 42 after sorting sites by identifier within each RTP. Only sites with reported positive point counts enter the median and noise calculation. Other sites supply zero quantified point-hours. These configured settings represent a reproducible background-use scenario, not measured utilisation or an independently validated forecast.

**Available Capacity:**

$$
C_{avail,{\ell}}=C_{daily,{\ell}}(1-U_{\ell}^{{bg}}){.}
$$ {#eq-available-capacity-app}

**Weighted Public Charging Demand:**

$$
D_\ell=\sum_{i,j,p}\frac{f_{ij}^{(p)}W^{(p)}R_{ij}}{o_p}\,t_{ij}
\left[s^O_{ij}\mathbf{1}\{a(i)=\ell\}+s^D_{ij}\mathbf{1}\{a(j)=\ell\}\right].
$$ {#eq-destination-demand-app}

The endpoint energy shares are defined with @eq-demand-definition. All eligible non-home trips contribute origin demand, and all eligible medium trips contribute destination demand. Their loads are pooled once at each physical site. Home charging is represented by the HCF threshold without a separate capacity test. The ancillary area-level public-reliance score $\rho_i$ does not discount these trip-specific loads.

**Available Capacity in Charging-Hours:**

$$
C_{avail,{\ell}}^{hours}=C_{avail,{\ell}}t_{session}\mathrel{=}{16}{n}_{\ell}{(}{1}\mathbin{-}{U}_{\ell}^{{bg}}{)}{.}
$$ {#eq-capacity-hours-app}

**Capacity Constraint:**

$$
Cap_k=\mathbf{1}\{a(k)\text{ exists},\ n_{a(k)}>0,\ D_{a(k)}\leq C_{avail,a(k)}^{hours}\},\quad k\in\{i,j\}.
$$ {#eq-capacity-constraint-app}

**Charging Bottleneck Detection:**

$$
B_{\ell}^{bottleneck}=\mathbf{1}\{D_{\ell}>C_{avail,{\ell}}^{hours}\}
$$ {#eq-bottleneck-capacity-app}

## A.7 EV Type Selection Factors {#sec-ev-type-selection-factors-appendix .unnumbered}

**Household Size Factor:**

$$
HSF_i = \frac{\sum_{k} (H_{k,i} \cdot w_{size,k} \cdot m_{car,k} \cdot m_{acc,k})}{H_{total,i}}
$$ {#eq-household-size-factor-app}

where $HSF_i$ represents household size factor, $H_{k,i}$ denotes household count for composition type $k$.

**Age Adjustment Factor:**

$$
AAF_i = \sum_{a} \left(\frac{P_{a,i}}{P_{total,i}} \cdot w_{age,a}\right)
$$ {#eq-age-adjustment-app}

where $AAF_i$ represents age adjustment factor, $P_{a,i}$ denotes population in age band $a$.

**Children Presence Factor:**

$$
CPF_i = \frac{H_{children,i}}{H_{total,i}}
$$ {#eq-children-factor-app}

where $CPF_i$ represents children factor, $H_{children,i}$ denotes households with dependent children.

**2-Seater Suitability Score:**

$$
S_{2-seater,i} = w_{hs} \cdot HSF_i + w_{age} \cdot AAF_i + w_{child} \cdot (1 - CPF_i)
$$ {#eq-two-seater-score-app}

where higher scores indicate greater suitability for compact 2-seater vehicles (small households, no children).

**4-Seater Suitability Score:**

$$
S_{4-seater,i} = w_{hs} \cdot (1 - HSF_i) + w_{age} \cdot (1 - AAF_i) + w_{child} \cdot CPF_i + \beta_{child} \cdot \mathbf{1}\{CPF_i > 0.2\}
$$ {#eq-four-seater-score-app}

where $\beta_{child}$ provides additional weighting for areas with significant child presence, favouring 4-seater vehicles.

## A.8 Output Aggregation {#sec-output-aggregation-appendix .unnumbered}

**Total Substitution Potential:**

$$
R_{total} = \sum_{i,j,p} N_{ij}^{(p)}
$$ {#eq-total-replacement-app}

**Total Daily Trips:**

$$
T_{total} = \sum_{i,j,p} f_{ij}^{(p)}
$$ {#eq-total-daily-trips-app}

**Vehicle Type Distribution:**

$$
Q_{type} = \frac{\sum_{i: EV\_type_i = type} \sum_{j,p} N_{ij}^{(p)}}{\sum_{i,j,p} N_{ij}^{(p)}}
$$ {#eq-vehicle-distribution-app}

# Appendix B: Parameter Assessment and Sensitivity Analysis {#app-sensitivity-calibration .unnumbered}

This appendix reports component-level parameter diagnostics and sensitivity analyses of the theoretical and capacity-sufficient substitution shares. The grids assess demographic weighting, social-grade scoring, home-charging feasibility, vehicle-type assignment, geographic adjustment, purpose suitability and interaction effects. Their interpretation depends on the scoring equation, sample, outcome and comparison criterion used in each exercise. The demographic--home-charging blend, accommodation--parking blend and interaction multipliers define the reference specification as modelling assumptions.

## B.1 Parameter Grid Summary {#sec-parameter-grid-summary-appendix .unnumbered}

@tbl-sensitivity-calibration summarises the component grids and specifications shown. @tbl-sensitivity-extended identifies the parameters varied and diagnostic metrics. Sensitivity of the theoretical and capacity-sufficient trip shares to AP-band boundaries, distance decay and purpose weights is reported separately in @tbl-band-edge-headline.
